```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false

library(psych)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

file.exists("data/processed_data/LR_h2_data.csv")

h1_data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/LR_h1_data.csv")

h2_data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/LR_h2_data.csv")
```

## Hypothesis 1

People with lower perceived social class will have more collectivist attitudes. 


### Variables and descriptive statistics

- **Self-reported social class: (`cot_class`):** A categorical variable with five groups: 1=Lower, 2=Lower middle, 3=Middle, 4=Upper middle, 5=Upper.
- **Average Collectivism (`collect_avg`):** Mean of three questions surrounding collectivist values, utilizing a 1-7 Likert scale. No reversal; higher scores indicate greater collectivism.

```{r}
#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1_data$cot_class)

# Summarize attractiveness points separately for each group.
by(h1_data$collect_avg, h1_data$cot_class, summary)
```

### Graph

@fig_collectivism shows the distribution of points by self-reported social class. The half-violin shows the shape of the distribution, the box summarizes the median and quartiles, and the dots represent individual responses.

```{r}
#| label: fig-collectivism
#| fig-cap: "Average collectivist values by self-reported social class."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(data = h1_data,
                       aes(x = cot_class,
                           y = collect_avg,
                           fill = cot_class)) +
  geom_rain(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "Self-Reported Social Class",
       y = "Average Belief in Collectivism",
       fill = "Social Class",
       title = "Average Belief in Collectivism by Self-Reported Social Class") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

```


## Hypothesis 2

People who value gender equality will report higher overall romantic love with their partner.

### Variables and descriptive statistics
  
- **Average belief in gender equality (`gen_eq_avg`):** A mean of three reverse-coded questions about gender equality. Scores range from 1 to 7; higher scores indicate greater endorsement of gender equality.

- **Overall romantic love (`love_avg`):** A mean of 15 Likert-type questions about romantic love, all 15 responses required. Each item ranges from 1 (Not at all) to 5 (Extremely); higher scores indicate greater romantic love.

```{r}
#| label: h2-descriptives
summary(h2_data[, c("gen_eq_avg", "love_avg")])
```

### Graph

@fig_love shows the relationship between belief in gender equality and overall experiences of romantic love. Points are jittered to make overlapping responses easier to see; the recorded scores are unchanged. The line summarizes the linear trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig_love
#| fig-cap: "Belief in gender equality and overall experience of romantic love."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(data = h2_data,
                       aes(x = gen_eq_avg,
                           y = love_avg
                           )) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0.04, alpha = 0.04, size = 0.6) +
  labs(x = "Average Belief in Gender Equality",
       y = "Average Experience of Overall Romantic Love",
       title = "Experience of Overall Romantic Love by Belief in Gender Equality") +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

```

### Observed trend

```{r}
#| label: correlation
r <- cor(h2_data$gen_eq_avg, h2_data$love_avg, use = "complete.obs")
round(r, 2)
```

The correlation was `{r} round(r, 2)`, indicating a weak negative association. Respondents who reported more confidence in finding a new partner tended to report lower commitment.
